item.title: U.S. stocks drift in mixed early trading on Wall Street as Apple falls
item.description: The U.S. stock market is drifting in mixed trading, with Apple falling but other stocks picking up the slack following strong profit reports.
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: FRANKFURT, Germany — The U.S. stock market is drifting in mixed trading, with Apple falling but other stocks picking up the slack following strong profit reports. The S&P 500 rose 0.2 per cent early Tuesday, though more stocks were falling than rising within the index. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 212 points, and the Nasdaq composite was up 0.5 per cent. Apple fell 3.2 per cent after saying it expects to make less profit from each $1 of its revenue during the final three months of this year. The price of Brent crude fell 1.7 per cent to $103 a barrel. Indexes were mixed in Europe and Asia. THIS IS A BREAKING NEWS UPDATE. Check back for updates. AP’s earlier story follows below. U.S. futures were mixed Tuesday ahead of the U.S. midterm elections and with concerns continuing to grow about the huge costs of expansion in the artificial intelligence sector. Oil prices rebounded from a sharp retreat to start the week after the United States conducted defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz. The outcome of Tuesday’s vote could fundamentally reshape President Donald Trump’s final two years in the White House. Republicans and Democrats are battling for control of Congress and key governors’ offices at a time of widespread disaffection over high prices. The futures for the S&P 500 fell less than 0.1 per cent and that for the Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 0.5 per cent. The Nasdaq composite gained 0.25 per cent. It’s been a mixed performance for indexes to start the week though the majority of stocks within the S&P 500 climbed as oil prices retreated. After falling nearly 8 per cent Monday, Brent crude rose almost 2 per cent to $106.50 per barrel early Tuesday after the U.S. attacked Iran’s Qeshm Island. U.S. benchmark crude tumbled 8 per cent to start the week, but rose 2 per cent to reach $98.49 per barrel Tuesday. Energy prices have been extremely vulnerable due to uncertainty over when the war with Iran will end. It has also been volatile for artificial-intelligence companies amid criticism that shares have surged too high and are in a bubble. Worries are growing that all the hundreds of billions of dollars Big Tech companies are pouring into AI data centers won’t yield enough productivity and profit to make the investments worth it. Apple, which has been perceived as a late-starter in the AI race, posted stronger-than-expected revenue in the fourth quarter after the bell Monday, but shares slid 4 per cent early Tuesday amid surging global demand for memory and expenses related to its release of Siri AI. Palantir also reported quarterly earnings after the bell. Its shares slumped 8 per cent in premarket trading after a slowdown for its U.S. commercial bookings. The latest profit reports from Alphabet and other Big Tech companies also showed how AI may be dragging on their own businesses. Google’s parent company burned through more cash during the latest quarter, as measured by free cash flow, and it reported slower-than-expected growth in its search business. Expectations are high for all kinds of companies to continue to deliver big gains in profits as the U.S. economy keeps chugging along, even with high inflation and elevated interest rates. That helped send the S&P 500 to a record high last month. In early European trading, the CAC 40 in Paris fell 0.2 per cent to 8,035.07, Britain’s FTSE 100 slid 0.5 per cent to 10,701.09, and Germany’s DAX declined 0.6 per cent to 25,830.22. In Asia, South Korea’s benchmark Kospi fell 4 per cent to 5,626.08. Memory chipmaker SK Hynix dropped 5.7 per cent and Samsung Electronics declined 4 per cent, giving up Monday’s gains. Markets in Tokyo were closed for a holiday. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng added 0.6 per cent to 23,525.97. The Shanghai Composite index retreated 0.8 per cent to 3,608.10, near its lowest level in more than a year. Gains from market-supporting measures announced Monday were short-lived. The U.S. dollar rose 0.2 per cent to 158.28 Japanese yen while the euro fell less than 1 per cent to $1.1179. ___ Rod McGuirk in Melbourne, Australia, contributed to this report. Elaine Lai, The Associated Press

item.title: XCCommerce Appoints Former Victoria’s Secret CIO Murali Sundararajan to Board of Directors
item.description: A leading provider of enterprise omnichannel promotion and incentive technology, announced the appointment of Murali Sundararajan to its board of directors.
item.dc:creator: Business Wire
item.content:encoded: This press release is provided by Business Wire and is published as received. MONTRÉAL--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- XCCommerce, a leading provider of enterprise omnichannel promotion and incentive technology, today announced the appointment of Murali Sundararajan to its board of directors. Sundararajan recently served as executive vice president and chief information officer of Victoria’s Secret & Co., following a distinguished tenure leading global technology strategy, digital transformation and enterprise innovation. Sundararajan’s appointment comes as retailers face growing pressure to deliver consistent, more personalized promotions across channels for a frictionless, seamless omnichannel shopping experience. His perspective as a CIO will help guide XCCommerce’s continued investment in innovation, AI-ready promotion capabilities and enterprise growth. Most recently, Sundararajan led the global technology strategy, cybersecurity and enterprise operations at Victoria’s Secret. During his decade-long tenure, he oversaw teams of more than 1,000 technology professionals supporting digital commerce and retail operations across more than 800 stores. His accomplishments include leading a more than $150 million digital and data transformation program encompassing e-commerce modernization, order management, pricing and promotions, and customer-facing platforms. Sundararajan also spent 15 years at Lowe’s Home Improvement, where he helped shape enterprise architecture and retail innovation, including a more than $680 million technology transformation across 1,800 stores. He currently serves as an advisor to Safe Security and an investor and advisor to Graphio.ai. “Murali brings an exceptional combination of retail technology expertise and firsthand knowledge of working with promotions, incentives and loyalty programs,” said Danny Rosenoff, CEO of XCCommerce. “Murali has been a valued and trusted partner over the years, and his insights will be invaluable as we accelerate innovation, expand our enterprise presence and help retailers modernize their promotion strategies.” “Flexible, scalable and reliable promotion technology is critical to a retailer’s business success,” Sundararajan said. “In this new era, where personalization, AI and omnichannel execution are transforming how consumers engage with retailers, XCCommerce sits in a leadership position, helping retailers navigate this evolution. I’m excited to work with their team and expand the company’s impact across retail.” About XCCommerce Inc. XCCommerce is a leading provider of enterprise retail promotion and incentive solutions, enabling retailers to create, manage and execute complex promotions, coupons, discounts and personalized offers across channels. Its flexible, scalable technology helps retailers simplify promotion execution, improve customer engagement and deliver seamless shopping experiences. With a commitment to “Incentives Without Limits,” XCCommerce empowers retailers to innovate without the constraints of legacy promotion systems. item.title: Panago Celebrates 40th Birthday With Throwback Deals and Customer Appreciation Day
item.description: Panago is turning 40, and the Canadian-owned pizza chain is celebrating four decades in business this November with throwback pizza deals.
item.dc:creator: Business Wire
item.content:encoded: This press release is provided by Business Wire and is published as received. ABBOTSFORD, British Columbia--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Panago is turning 40, and the Canadian-owned pizza chain is celebrating four decades in business this November with throwback pizza deals and a birthday party to thank the customers and communities who have been part of its journey. Founded in Abbotsford, B.C., in 1986, Panago has grown from a small pizza operation into a national chain with 170 locations, more than 140 franchisee partners and an estimated 2,750 corporate and franchise employees. Today, the company sells over six million pizzas annually. “Our 40th birthday is an opportunity to thank the customers, franchisees and communities who have been part of Panago’s journey,” said Sean DeGregorio, CEO. “We’re proud of how far we’ve come and excited to celebrate this milestone with the people who helped make it possible.” From Nov. 3–30, customers can celebrate with two limited-time offers: Both offers are available at Panago locations in B.C., Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario and Yukon, for delivery, pickup or in-store ordering. Taxes and delivery fees are extra; offers are not available through third-party delivery apps. The celebrations culminate in Panago’s Birthday Party and Customer Appreciation Day on Sunday, November 29, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. At participating locations, customers can walk in for a 12-inch medium Tropical Hawaiian, Garden Veggie, New York Deli, BBQ Bacon Chicken, or Panago Classic pizza for just $5.99. Daiya Dairy-Free Cheese is available for substitution, and Gluten-smart crust is available at an additional charge. No other substitutions. Taxes and restrictions apply. For offer details or to find a location, visit panago.com. About PanagoFounded in 1986, Panago Pizza is a privately held Canadian pizza and delivery chain with 170 locations nationwide. Panago offers pizzas, sides, and desserts, and is known for its customizable menu, inclusive options, and delicious flavour combinations. Learn more or order at panago.com.
